title: Vertical Angles Theorem
summary: When two lines intersect, each pair of vertical angles is congruent.
proofIdea: When two lines cross, each vertical angle and its adjacent angle form a straight angle. Angles that complete the same straight angle are equal, so the opposite angles match.
explorationPrompt: In this diagram, move O, L, or M and compare the two opposite angle pairs as the lines rotate and shift.

proofSteps.title: Adjacent angles form a straight angle
proofSteps.detail: Each vertical angle sits next to a neighboring angle on a straight line, so each adjacent pair makes a straight angle.

proofSteps.title: Both pairs complete the same straight angle
proofSteps.detail: If one opposite angle and the shared adjacent angle make a straight angle, and the other opposite angle with that same adjacent angle also makes a straight angle, then both sums are equal.

proofSteps.title: Subtract the shared adjacent angle
proofSteps.detail: Since the shared adjacent angle appears in both equal sums, removing it leaves the two vertical angles congruent.

proofSteps.title: Repeat for the other pair
proofSteps.detail: The same argument works for the remaining opposite pair, so both vertical-angle pairs are congruent.
